notExpressible.name: records.get
notExpressible.why: The generator's types are string, int, bool, string[], and void. It has no nullable result. Listing this method next to records.delete would also emit struct RecordId twice: a params name cannot be shared. iOS and Android use the RecordId generated for records.delete. The method stays in src/ui/host.ts.

notExpressible.name: files.takeOpened
notExpressible.why: No object type and no array of objects. Swift and Kotlin output is parameter structs only, not Encodable result types, so OpenedFile stays hand-written in the app shells. The method stays in src/ui/host.ts.

notExpressible.name: files.opened
notExpressible.why: Event data has no null (or other payload-less) type. HostEvents in src/ui/host.ts stays hand-written. The app calls emit(event) with no payload.
